title: Plan spaced repetition realistically
description: Create a flexible review schedule using retrieval practice and adjustment after errors.
accomplishes: Create a flexible review schedule using retrieval practice and adjustment after errors. Prioritise difficult material without inventing a universal retention curve. Include short checks and clear rules for rescheduling when the learner misses a session.
prompt:
Act as a learning coach.

Task: Plan spaced repetition realistically.

Input context:
- MATERIAL: [MATERIAL]
- EXAM OR GOAL: [EXAM OR GOAL]
- AVAILABLE TIME: [AVAILABLE TIME]
- CURRENT DIFFICULTIES: [CURRENT DIFFICULTIES]

Create a flexible review schedule using retrieval practice and adjustment after errors. Prioritise difficult material without inventing a universal retention curve. Include short checks and clear rules for rescheduling when the learner misses a session.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Review schedule proposal
Introduce a small set of cards, revisit them after a short interval and bring difficult items back sooner. Mix recall with an application question instead of repeatedly rereading the answer. Adjust the next review using actual performance. The schedule is a starting hypothesis, not a guarantee of retention or an evidence-based personal forgetting model.
